register.name: UNHCR Iran, 2026 requirements
register.detail: UNHCR · Iran Emergency Fact Sheet, April 2026 · 15% funded, US$20.7M, at 30 April 2026 · US$119.3M unfunded
register.note: Iran hosts 1.65 million refugees and others in need of international protection, the majority Afghans
register.text: The funds UNHCR requests for its work in Iran in 2026, for refugees and others in need of international protection; at 30 April 2026 the request was 15% funded. From 1 March to 30 April 2026, UNHCR assisted 102,200 people, including with multipurpose cash, gave core relief items to 1,500 conflict-affected households and distributed 127,000 medicine kits for non-communicable diseases. It serves the health and livelihood standards of refugee families.

register.name: Iran Flash Refugee Response Plan, March to May 2026
register.detail: UNHCR and partners · launched 26 March 2026 · ran March to May 2026 · 2.8 million people in Iran · UNHCR requirements US$36.23M
register.note: An inter-agency plan for refugees and others in need of international protection, and affected host communities
register.text: An inter-agency plan launched on 26 March 2026, seeking US$80 million to provide protection and life-saving assistance to 2.8 million people in Iran from March to May 2026. It targets refugees and others in need of international protection, and the host communities affected. Life-saving assistance reaches the food, water, shelter and health standards of families displaced or hosted in Iran.

register.name: Emergency Appeal for the Iranian Red Crescent response (MDRIR018)
register.detail: IFRC · launched 10 March 2026 · appeal code MDRIR018
register.note: Supports the emergency response of the Iranian Red Crescent Society
register.text: An emergency appeal of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies for CHF 40 million, launched on 10 March 2026, to support the response of the Iranian Red Crescent Society. It is the Red Cross and Red Crescent channel for humanitarian relief to people affected by the emergency, for needs that cannot wait.

register.name: EU contribution to WFP food assistance in Iran
register.detail: European Union · World Food Programme release of 26 July 2026 · 12 months · 52,000 people, 17,000 Iranians and 35,000 refugees
register.note: Cash-based transfers, school feeding programmes and livelihood support
register.text: A contribution of €3.08 million from the European Union to the World Food Programme in Iran, sustaining assistance over 12 months for vulnerable refugees and conflict-affected Iranians. WFP plans to reach 52,000 people, 17,000 Iranians and 35,000 refugees, with cash-based transfers, school feeding programmes and livelihood support. It serves the food standard, and education and livelihood through school meals and livelihood support.

register.name: Japan Emergency Grant, share for Iran
register.detail: Government of Japan · decided 26 June 2026 · UNHCR US$4M, IFRC US$2.5M, WFP US$2M, ICRC US$1.5M · part of US$15M for Iran, Lebanon and Palestine
register.note: Food, health and medical care, non-food items, and water, sanitation and hygiene
register.text: Of an Emergency Grant of US$15 million that the Government of Japan decided on 26 June 2026 for Iran, Lebanon and Palestine, US$10 million is for Iran, through UNHCR, the IFRC, the World Food Programme and the ICRC. It funds non-food items, water, sanitation and hygiene and health through UNHCR, health and medical care through the IFRC and the ICRC, and food through WFP. It serves the food, water and health standards.

register.name: Strengthening Disaster Resilience of Critical Medical Infrastructure (BEHTAB III)
register.detail: Government of Japan and UN-Habitat · Exchange of Notes signed 20 February 2026 · grant of ¥910M, about US$5.9M
register.note: Retrofitting health facilities and integrating green and solar energy solutions
register.text: A grant of ¥910 million, about US$5.9 million, from the Government of Japan to UN-Habitat, to restore safe, resilient and functional health infrastructure across Iran by retrofitting health facilities and integrating green and solar energy solutions. It builds on two earlier projects that followed the 2017 earthquake in Kermanshah province. It serves the health standard, by keeping hospitals working when earthquakes and climate hazards strike.
